chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about dates and raisins being cooked for Nabeez, so he said: 'No'. And he said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited'. And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whatever the large quantity of it intoxicates, the small quantity of it is prohibited'. And he said: 'Yeast is not suitable for Nabeez, and it is the turbid (cloudy) substance'.

key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: Nabeez, a traditional fermented drink made from dates or raisins

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Nabeez and the role of yeast in its fermentation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic principle of 'kathiruhu wa qaliluhu' (abundance and scarcity) in determining the prohibition of Nabeez, a pre-Islamic fermented beverage. It highlights the specific exclusion of 'khamirah' (yeast/turbid sediment) as a contaminant that affects the drink's purity and intoxicating potential, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both the substance and the method of fermentation in legal rulings.
